definitions.TREE: Fast growing function based on Kruskal's tree theorem.
definitions.LEAF: The usually green and flat organ that represents the most prominent feature of most vegetative plants.
definitions.ROOT: The part of a plant, generally underground, that anchors and supports the plant body, absorbs and stores water and nutrients, and in some plants is able to perform vegetative reproduction.
definitions.BARK: The short, loud, explosive sound uttered by a dog, a fox, and some other animals.
definitions.WOOD: The substance making up the central part of the trunk and branches of a tree.
definitions.MOSS: Any of various small, green, seedless plants growing on the ground or on the surfaces of trees, stones, etc.
definitions.FERN: Any of a group of some twenty thousand species of vascular plants classified in the division Pteridophyta that lack seeds and reproduce by shedding spores to initiate an alternation of generations.
definitions.BUSH: A woody plant distinguished from a tree by its multiple stems and lower height, being usually less than six metres tall.
definitions.VINE: The climbing plant that produces grapes.
definitions.SAND: Rock that is ground more finely than gravel, but is not as fine as silt (more formally, see grain sizes chart), forming beaches and deserts and also used in construction.
definitions.CLAY: A mineral substance made up of small crystals of silica and alumina, that is ductile when moist.
definitions.SOIL: A mixture of mineral particles and organic material, used to support plant growth.
definitions.HILL: An elevated location smaller than a mountain.
definitions.CAVE: A large, naturally-occurring cavity formed underground or in the face of a cliff or a hillside.
definitions.GLEN: A secluded and narrow valley, especially one with a river running through it.
definitions.LAKE: A small stream of running water; a channel for water; a drain.
definitions.POND: An inland body of standing water, either natural or man-made, that is smaller than a lake.
definitions.POOL: A small and rather deep collection of (usually) fresh water, as one supplied by a spring, or occurring in the course of a stream; a reservoir for water.
definitions.RIVER: A large and often winding stream which drains a land mass, carrying water down from higher areas to a lower point, oftentimes ending in another body of water, such as an ocean or in an inland sea.
definitions.BROOK: To use; enjoy; have the full employment of.
definitions.CREEK: A small inlet or bay, often saltwater, narrower and extending farther into the land than a cove; a recess in the shore of the sea, or of a river; the inner part of a port that is used as a dock for small boats.
definitions.OCEAN: One of the large bodies of water separating the continents.
definitions.SEA: A large body of salt water.
definitions.WAVE: To move back and forth repeatedly and somewhat loosely.
definitions.TIDE: The periodic change of the sea level, particularly when caused by the gravitational influence of the sun and the moon.
definitions.RAIN: Condensed water falling from a cloud.
definitions.SNOW: The frozen, crystalline state of water that falls as precipitation.
definitions.HAIL: Balls or pieces of ice falling as precipitation, often in connection with a thunderstorm.
definitions.DEW: Any moisture from the atmosphere condensed by cool bodies upon their surfaces.
definitions.MIST: Water or other liquid finely suspended in air.
definitions.FOG: A thick cloud that forms near the ground; the obscurity of such a cloud.
definitions.WIND: Real or perceived movement of atmospheric air usually caused by convection or differences in air pressure.
definitions.STORM: Any disturbed state of the atmosphere, especially as affecting the earth's surface, and strongly implying destructive or unpleasant weather.
definitions.SUN: A star, especially when seen as the centre of any single solar system.
definitions.MOON: The Earth's moon Luna; the sole natural satellite of the Earth, represented in astronomy and astrology by ☾.
definitions.STAR: Any small luminous dot appearing in the cloudless portion of the night sky, especially with a fixed location relative to other such dots.
definitions.SKY: The atmosphere above a given point, especially as visible from the ground during the day.
definitions.DAWN: The morning twilight period immediately before sunrise.
definitions.DUSK: A period of time at the end of day when the sun is below the horizon but before the full onset of night, especially the darker part of twilight.
definitions.NIGHT: The period between sunset and sunrise, when a location faces far away from the sun, thus when the sky is dark.
definitions.DARK: Having an absolute or (more often) relative lack of light.
definitions.MOUNTAIN: A large natural elevation of the earth's surface rising abruptly from the surrounding level.
definitions.FOREST: A large area covered chiefly with trees and undergrowth.
definitions.JUNGLE: A large, undeveloped, humid forest, especially in a tropical region, that is home to many wild plants and animals; a tropical rainforest.
definitions.DESERT: A dry, sandy region with little rainfall and sparse vegetation.
definitions.ISLAND: A contiguous area of land, smaller than a continent, totally surrounded by water.
definitions.CANYON: A deep gorge, typically one with a river flowing through it.
definitions.VALLEY: A low area of land between hills or mountains, typically with a river.
definitions.PLATEAU: A largely level expanse of land at a high elevation; tableland.
definitions.PRAIRIE: An extensive area of relatively flat grassland with few, if any, trees, especially in North America.
definitions.MEADOW: A field of grass, often wildflowers, used for pasture or solace.
definitions.GLACIER: A slowly moving mass or river of ice formed by the accumulation of snow.
definitions.VOLCANO: A vent or fissure on the surface of a planet (usually in a mountainous form) with a magma chamber attached to the mantle of a planet or moon, periodically erupting forth lava and volcanic gases onto the surface.
definitions.GEYSER: A boiling natural spring which throws forth at frequent intervals jets of water, mud etc., driven up by the expansive power of steam.
definitions.WATERFALL: A flow of water over the edge of a cliff.
definitions.SPRINGS: To weaken, as a joint, ligament, or muscle, by sudden and excessive exertion, as by wrenching; to overstrain, or stretch injuriously, but without luxation.
definitions.MARSH: An area of low, wet land, often with tall grass.
definitions.SWAMP: A piece of wet, spongy land; low ground saturated with water; soft, wet ground which may have a growth of certain kinds of trees, but is unfit for agricultural or pastoral purposes.
definitions.BOG: An area of decayed vegetation (particularly sphagnum moss) which forms a wet spongy ground too soft for walking; a marsh or swamp.
definitions.TUNDRA: A vast, flat, treeless Arctic region where the subsoil is permanently frozen.
definitions.STEPPE: The grasslands of Eastern Europe and Asia.
definitions.RAINFOREST: A forest in a climate with high annual rainfall and no dry season.
definitions.SAVANNAH: A tropical grassland with scattered trees.
definitions.MANGROVE: Any of various tropical evergreen trees or shrubs that grow in shallow coastal water.
definitions.REEF: A chain or range of rocks, sand, or coral lying at or near the surface of the water.
definitions.ATOLL: A type of island consisting of a ribbon reef that nearly or entirely surrounds a lagoon and supports, in most cases, one to many islets on the reef platform.
definitions.PENINSULA: A piece of land projecting into water from a larger land mass.
definitions.CONTINENT: Each of the main continuous land-masses on the earth's surface, now generally regarded as seven in number, including their related islands, continental shelves etc.
definitions.PLANET: Each of the seven major bodies which move relative to the fixed stars in the night sky—the Moon, Mercury, Venus, the Sun, Mars, Jupiter and Saturn.
definitions.ATMOSPHERE: The gases surrounding the Earth or any astronomical body.
definitions.BIOSPHERE: The part of the Earth and its atmosphere capable of supporting life.
definitions.ECOSYSTEM: A system formed by an ecological community and its environment that functions as a unit.
definitions.HABITAT: Conditions suitable for an organism or population of organisms to live.
definitions.WILDLIFE: Animals, plants, and fungi, not normally domesticated, often to the exclusion of plants, fungi, fish, insects and other invertebrates, and microscopic plants and animals; hence:.
definitions.FLORA: Plants considered as a group, especially those of a particular country, region, time, etc.
definitions.FAUNA: Animals considered as a group; especially those of a particular country, region, time.
definitions.SURVIVAL: The fact or act of surviving.
definitions.CLIMATE: An area of the earth's surface between two parallels of latitude.
definitions.WEATHER: The short term state of the atmosphere at a specific time and place, including the temperature, relative humidity, cloud cover, precipitation, wind, etc.
definitions.SEASON: Each of the four divisions of a year: spring, summer, autumn (fall) and winter.
definitions.SPRING: To weaken, as a joint, ligament, or muscle, by sudden and excessive exertion, as by wrenching.
definitions.SUMMER: One of four seasons, traditionally the second, marked by the longest and typically hottest days of the year due to the inclination of the Earth and thermal lag.
definitions.AUTUMN: Traditionally the third of the four seasons, when deciduous trees lose their leaves.
definitions.WINTER: Traditionally the fourth of the four seasons, typically regarded as being from December 23 to March 20 in continental regions of the Northern Hemisphere or the months of June, July and August in the Southern Hemisphere.
definitions.EQUINOX: The intersection of the apparent path of the sun in the sky (the ecliptic) with the celestial equator.
definitions.SOLSTICE: One of the two points in the ecliptic at which the sun is furthest from the celestial equator.
definitions.ECLIPSE: An alignment of astronomical objects whereby one object comes between the observer (or notional observer) and another object, thus obscuring the latter.
